name: fleet100_r02
prompt:
One image: a sprite sheet of 9 cars for a 2D top-down city game.

THE VIEW MUST BE EXACTLY OVERHEAD. These cars were drawn before as if seen a little from one side: the lower flank's doors, sills and side windows showed below the roof, and the roof sat above the middle of the body. Draw each one from directly above the middle of its roof, like a plan drawing: the roof centred across the body's width, and neither flank seen more than the other. Worn paint and rust may differ side to side; the view may not.

THE BODIES MUST BE SLIMMER. The previous attempt drew the view right but several cars too wide for their length. Measured against the sizes listed: car 1 about 16% too wide, car 4 14%, car 7 19%, car 8 12%, car 9 12%. Draw every body to its listed proportion, its flanks straight and close together; leave the extra room in each grid place empty rather than filling it with a wider car. Car 9 (4.90 m) is still drawn half as long again as car 1 (3.20 m), all at one scale.

Style: match the attached picture's art style exactly — outline weight, shading, highlights, level of detail, pixel size.

View: straight down from directly above the middle of each roof, orthographic, as the attached cars are: the roof centred across the body, and neither flank seen more than the other — no doors, sills or side windows showing along one side. No perspective, no ground, no shadow.

Layout: a 3×3 grid, the cars in the order listed, left to right and top to bottom. Each car lies horizontally with its nose to the right, centred in its place, with empty space round it. One shared scale for all.

Every car:
- Its length and width as listed, in that proportion, with straight flanks. Narrow cars stay narrow: leave spare room empty rather than draw a car wider.
- Its shape mirror-symmetric about its long centre line, with two small side mirrors just ahead of the windscreen; wear, rust and odd panels may differ side to side.
- Roof on. No tyres or wheels (the game draws them), no people, no text, logos, badges or licence plates.

Background: fully transparent outside the cars — no colour, no glow or halo, no shadow. Each car's edge ends sharply.

The cars in the picture only show the style: draw the cars listed, in their own colours. They are drawn at one scale, as the sheet's cars are: a longer car there is a longer drawing.
- Lamps switched off (unlit glass, no glow). Front corner: a headlamp and, beside it, a separate amber indicator. Rear corner: three separate small lenses side by side, each in its own thin dark frame, as distinct as the front's — red tail and brake lamp outermost, amber indicator next, white reversing lamp innermost. The rear indicator is the same amber as the front one and as large, plainly not red. Never one merged red cluster, never a light bar across the car.
- Condition shows only in the paint (faded colour, rust spots, a panel in another shade); the body outline is whole.

Cars, body length × width without mirrors, and what each is:
1. 3.20 × 1.42 m (2.25× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — 1990s Russian tiny three-door microcar, worn: faded red paint, rust spots on the sills, short flat bonnet, upright boxy cabin, flat roof, upright hatch, small rectangular headlamps, small square tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens. Last time 16% too wide: a narrow little box.
2. 3.50 × 1.50 m (2.33× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — late-1990s Korean tiny five-door city car, average condition, bright yellow, short round bonnet, tall rounded roof, short upright hatchback tail, big round-edged headlamps, small vertical tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
3. 3.50 × 1.50 m (2.33× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — late-1990s Korean tiny five-door city car, worn: faded pale green paint, rust spots on the wheel arches, short round bonnet, tall rounded roof, short upright hatchback tail, big round-edged headlamps, small vertical tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
4. 3.73 × 1.49 m (2.50× longer than wide), rounded corners — 1960s Soviet rear-engined two-door small saloon, worn: faded sky blue paint, rust spots, a rounded humped body, short sloping front lid, rounded roof, long rear deck over the engine with air intake slots on its sides, chrome bumpers, round headlamps, small tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens. Last time 14% too wide: slim and long.
5. 3.74 × 1.68 m (2.23× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — Soviet three-door small 4×4, average condition, olive green, boxy with flat panels, short flat bonnet, upright cab with a flat roof, squared tail, black plastic wheel-arch trims, round headlamps in a flat grille, small square tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens
6. 4.21 × 1.65 m (2.55× longer than wide), nearly square corners — 1990s Soviet wedge four-door saloon, worn: faded cherry red paint, rust spots on the sills and boot, low sloping wedge bonnet tapering to a narrow nose, the cabin set well back, a short high separate boot (not a square three-box classic), black plastic bumpers, slim rectangular headlamps, wide flat tail lamps split into red, amber and white sections
7. 4.25 × 1.55 m (2.74× longer than wide), nearly square corners — 1970s Soviet small four-door saloon, worn: faded teal paint, rust patches, a straight-edged body, flat bonnet, upright cabin, separate boot, chrome bumpers, rectangular headlamps, vertical tail lamps split into red, amber and white sections. Last time 19% too wide: the slimmest car on the sheet for its length, nearly three times longer than wide.
8. 4.36 × 1.94 m (2.25× longer than wide), rounded corners — Soviet forward-control 4×4 minibus, worn: faded grey paint with rust at the corners. Seen from above it has no bonnet at all: the windscreen starts right at the front edge of the body, and behind it one long smooth domed roof, curving down to every edge like a loaf of bread, with no ribs, rails or panels on it; the flat front face holds two round headlamps, small tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens. Last time 12% too wide.
9. 4.90 × 1.90 m (2.58× longer than wide), gently rounded corners — modern mid-size passenger van, good condition, white, short sloping bonnet, long tall body with a flat roof, big square tailgate, large headlamps, tall tail lamps; each rear lamp with a separate amber indicator lens and a white reversing lens. Last time 12% too wide: long and slim.
